These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

title: Empty formal-source file

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

Excluding it from derived search indexes cannot remove mathematical content. The path remains present in the authoritative source checkout and in the filtering ledger.
title: Empty formal-source file

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

title: Empty formal-source file

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. In books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp the quote and semicolon characters found by a naive grep belong to pipe-escaped symbol names for Java lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|), not to string literals or comments; a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 4 files individually scanned end to end (full read for the two under 50000 bytes, head/tail sampling plus targeted line-content checks for the two larger ones) with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.
books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp: grep -n for lines starting with ';' returned no matches, ruling out comment content despite nonzero raw semicolon/quote character counts.

evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.

Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/abstract-syntax-trees@useless-runes.lsp (2253885 bytes, largest) and books/kestrel/c/syntax/tests/.sys/types-to-tynames@useless-runes.lsp (47 bytes, smallest): individually checked, same result.

A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.
title: ACL2 useless-runes proof metadata retained

justification: A zero-byte source-language file contains no declaration, theorem statement, proof, comment, identifier, or other searchable text. Excluding it from derived search indexes cannot remove mathematical content. The path remains present in the authoritative source checkout and in the filtering ledger.
